analysis: The PR is documentation-only. It changes docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (new paragraph at head lines 508-514) and docs/architecture/inference.md (date bump and a new shape-warmup section after line 953). No executable code, wire protocol, key handling, attestation, authorization or encryption paths change, so no TB-002/TB-009/TB-011 control is altered. The text describes a provider-local startup shape warmup. It runs excluded probes under the same idle gate, foreground lease, KV and service budgets. It publishes no observations or work totals and does not change capacity wire fields. It adds a 20-second wall budget and a 128-token greedy probe. The startup preload runs before registration, so routed traffic cannot preempt it. Security-relevant observations: (1) The warmup uses synthetic prompts, so it does not touch A-001 consumer plaintext. The docs do not say whether a warmup could donate to the SSD prefix cache (T-041). The synthetic prompts are not consumer data, so I did not treat this as a finding, but the actual code should be checked to confirm warmup requests do not populate the cache under a shared or guessable cacheSalt. (2) The warmup pauses the proactive MLX pool sweep while a session runs, and on-pressure reclaims still run. This touches memory/availability (T-029, T-010), but the docs state the invariants are preserved. (3) The docs describe the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP env override, which can only restore plain probes or skip the shader-cache probe. That is an operator-local setting with no trust-boundary impact. Because only docs were supplied, the behavior claims are unverified against code. The next pass should check the shape-warmup implementation if it is in another batch, covering the posture-gate skip, the preemption handling and the prefix-cache interaction.
